title: Set each person's mug handle-first for their dominant hand
instruction: The person at the green placemat is left-handed and the person at the yellow placemat is right-handed. Set a mug on each placemat so each person can pick it up by the handle.
context: Serving people, as in care or hospitality, means turning each cup to suit their hand. Both people face the robot, so their left is the robot's right, and the two answers are opposite.
setup: Two placemats (14 x 16 cm) lie 32 cm in front of the arm bases, a green one 10 cm left of their midline and a yellow one 10 cm right of it; a person would sit beyond each, facing the robot. Two red ceramic mugs (8.5 cm across with the handle, 6 cm tall, 0.3 kg) stand 18 cm in front of the bases, 20 cm left and 20 cm right of the midline, handles pointing straight at the robot.
scoring: 0 if a mug ever tilts more than 30 degrees. For each placemat: 0.5 if an upright mug (within 15 degrees) stands on it with its handle within 30 degrees of that person's dominant hand (green: the robot's right; yellow: the robot's left), 0.1 if a mug on it faces elsewhere, 0 if none.
reset_notes: Stand the mugs back on their marks with the handles pointing at the robot.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only; the mugs are empty. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2). No people are simulated; the placemats mark where they sit.
